items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了贝宁音乐人Antoine Dougbé与Poly-Rythmo乐队1977至1982年的合作录音。Dougbé被称作"魔鬼首相"，以拍腿演奏Cavacha节奏闻名，这一节奏由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车节奏中提取，后广泛流传于七十年代中期的刚果流行音乐。乐评指出，与乐队以往发行相比，此合辑的古巴son影响更为明显，尤其在前几首作品中，而刚果伦巴的渗透同样可辨。以《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》为例，开场以合成器铺底，吉他音色带有八十年代的塑料质感，镲片节奏贯穿始终，中段吉他开始向不同方向发展，合成器再次浮现形成底层纹理。《We Tayi Sin Assi Tche》则更直接地呈现古巴风格，稳定的牛铃节奏、经典鼻音唱腔与密集重复的吉他构成核心。整体保留了七十年代的根基，但录音与音色已随时代转向。Analog Africa作为专门挖掘非洲小众音乐的厂牌，长期致力于为Poly-Rythmo争取国际认可，此合辑是该系列的延续。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 乐队的第二张专辑以自制乐器为核心特色，所有演奏器具均由废旧物品与零碎材料手工打造，涵盖 tassofons、kitchenofon 等命名奇异的自制乐器。在高质量录音条件下，这些器物展现出出乎意料的准确音准与丰富音色。音乐风格上呈现高度融合特征：克莱兹默曲目以笑般声线演绎单簧管旋律，昆比亚作品配以西班牙合唱与拉丁打击乐，标题曲沉浸于非洲节拍的木鱼与摇铃，桑巴律动与中东迷幻旋律亦穿插其中。整张专辑通过即兴段落展示出深厚的演奏功底，跨越多种文化音乐传统，以废料为材却传达出节奏、旋律与和声超越物质局限的普世理念。

items.body: Carmen Villain Memoria New Carmen Villain shares its slow-burning intensity with the Apichatpong Weerasethakul film it shares a title with Memoria by Carmen Villain Carmen Villain’s fifth album, Memoria begins in familiar territory: flute tones stretch out across an enormous, reverberant field, the same patient sound that defined her last record. It doesn't stay there long. Within a couple of minutes the ground shifts, and the record makes its real statement: this is not music built for casual listening. Sharing its title with Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s languorous 2021 film, this is a record made for the kind of slow, attentive surrender that lets its details bloom. Where 2022’s Only Love from Now On found Villain working in a spectral, dub-inflected haze, Memoria pushes that language somewhere... The post Carmen Villain – Memoria appeared first on The Quietus.

items.body: Review by alainPP — Side 1 opens with "Do What U Will," a surprising electro-gothic track?echoes of Ultravox with vocals reminiscent of Alice Cooper. A welcome return to contemporary rock after a six-year hiatus. "Hey Humanity" returns to a signature sound, with faint traces of Bowie and the Beatles. Colorful keyboards meet a Led Zeppelin-esque vibe?a Xavier trademark?alongside a desire to soar on symphonic elements reminiscent of ELO and sparkling guitar work. A vibrant finale featuring Queen-style guitar?magnificent, yet all too brief. "Driving To Destruction" features percussive piano � la Sheller, staccato drums, and melancholic, U2-esque guitars. It's all here: a dash of XTC and ELO, backing vocals, Supertramp-style piano, Rogue Male-style guitar, and distinctive vocal phrasing. The dynamic lyrics hint at a crash far more serious than it initially appears. "Stay With Me" follows, with vocals melting into a haughty melody amidst a blend of synth pads and keyboards. The lyrics suggest a call to action?rolling up one's sleeves to save Gaia?delivered with a Beatles-esque, crossover sound. Then comes "Charlie Knew," echoing the great Lou Reed; an epic, operatic track with symphonic orchestration. It offers a somber reflection on the times as they descend into darkness, featuring a vintage Bowie vibe and a soaring, lyrical passage that channels Cooper's madness and ELO's hope?a concentrated dose of prog.Side B opens with "Siren In The Storm," an acoustic Western-style ballad played by Kaitlin?a song of being lost amidst the waves. Captivating, narrative vocals tell the story of a siren meant to save the hero; Savannah's moving voice evokes *The Dark Side of the Moon* before a melancholic solo launches "Enigmatic Terminus." That track takes flight with sharp violins, languid vocals, and radiant, U2-style electric guitar. It is a dark, metallic tale of an approaching end, driven by a linear, martial rhythm. "Legend of Mary Jo" is a charismatic track?an old-fashioned tune with an epic, old-world duration. It tells a sad, sordid tale of love in which the heroine stays with her unfaithful husband?a parable for our own disheartened society. Originally written early in his career while playing with The Sun Machine, it is a conceptual piece?reminiscent of the Beatles and Alice Cooper?featuring classical instruments and trumpets. It has a jovial, vibrant feel?I'm sticking with the Sparks-like synth comparison?alongside a colorful, Supertramp-esque saxophone drift and a soaring, Pink Floyd-style atmosphere; a gravelly vocal cuts through a choppy, Yes-style riff and its rock-oriented variations. It boasts a distinctive sound and a solemn finale that evokes the woman's incredible destiny. A track worthy of the prog giants, featuring a blissful, final Mellotron flourish.Phideaux returns, taking his time?true to his fundamental approach. It is an epic journey best experienced in the car?a blend of psychedelic folk and progressive rock that reveals itself to be far more complex and intricate than it initially seems.

items._cn_summary: Phideaux六年沉寂后回归之作，以跨界前卫摇滚为底色，融合交响编排、电古德暗色调与迷幻民谣元素。专辑分两面铺陈：A面以电子哥特开篇，随后以华丽键盘主导的旋律摇滚铺展，引用从披头士到齐柏林飞艇、ELO的多重参照，呈现繁复的编曲层次与Queen式吉他闪光；B面转向更沉郁的叙事，以原声西部民谣开场，逐步过渡到金属质感的黑暗叙事，末曲以古典乐器、小号与梅洛特朗收束，兼具史诗长度与概念统一性。整体制作展现出对70年代摇滚遗产的熟稔致敬，同时融入当代环境议题的歌词指向。虽以摇滚传统为核心，但在管弦配器与情绪跨度上展现一定艺术野心，适合偏好渐进式结构与古典摇滚融合的听众。

items.body: San Jacinto, up in the Montes de María on Colombia’s Caribbean side, had a dancer called Magdalena Ruiz. The gaiteros remembered her white smile and the grace in the way she moved, and how a gathering lifted the moment she arrived: the musicians, the dancers, the drinking, the young and the old. Adolfo Pacheco remembered her too: “Si no llegaba Magdalena, se enfriaba de la gaita el son”. If she failed to arrive, the gaitas went cold. “Ahora la evoco en mi cantar”, he sings, now I call her up in my song. Those gatherings take the shape of a rueda de cumbia. The musicians stand in the middle and the women dance around them, candles in hand, long skirts sweeping the ground. Caja and gaita set the pace and the circle follows. When Magdalena arrived, that circle opened for her. “Magdalena Ruiz” opens Madre Cumbia, the album Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto, Fruko and Carmelo Torres release on 20 October through the San Diego label Bad Vibes Good Friends. Ten songs, most of them from the sabanera repertoire: three by Andrés Landero, one Torres wrote himself, the rest from writers like Rafael Pérez and Betty Ochoa. Los Gaiteros have carried the gaitas of San Jacinto since the 1940s. Fruko was the bassist and producer who ran the golden era of Discos Fuentes. Carmelo Torres took the accordion straight from Andrés Landero, his teacher and the man who made cumbia sabanera. Between them they hold most of what happened to cumbia in the last eighty years, and this is the first time the three of them have been in a studio together. They recorded in Bogotá with nine musicians in the room, Rory Morison producing and Gabriel Torregrosa directing. On “Magdalena Ruiz” the melody belongs to Iván Salcedo‘s gaita corta, the short flute a San Jacinto cumbia is built on, and Carmelo Torres answers on accordion while Fruko holds the bass underneath. Behind them, caja, conga, guacharaca and maracas keep the rueda turning, and Rafael Castro sings the lead. Listen to “Magdalena Ruiz” and pre-order Madre Cumbia HERE The post Daily Discovery: Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto x Carmelo Torres x Fruko y Sus Tesos – Magdalena Ruiz appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于哥伦比亚加勒比海岸传统cumbia sabanera专辑《Madre Cumbia》的乐评。专辑由三位资深音乐人合作录制：自1940年代起传承gaita笛子演奏的Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto、Discos Fuentes黄金时期的贝斯手兼制作人Fruko、以及从Andrés Landero处习得手风琴技艺的Carmelo Torres，这是三人首次同入录音室。文章聚焦主打曲目《Magdalena Ruiz》，以Adolfo Pacheco的诗句开头，讲述一位名叫Magdalena的舞者如何令gaita乐声焕发生机。录音于波哥大完成，九位乐手同场演奏，Iván Salcedo的gaita corta短笛主导旋律，Torres以手风琴应答，Fruko担任贝斯，caja、conga、guacharaca与maracas维持rueda de cumbia圆圈舞的节奏脉动，整张专辑十首曲目大多来自sabanera曲目库，由Andrés Landero等多位词曲作者创作。

items.body: Words by Justin TurfordThe iconic ‘Future Sounds of Jazz’ series has reached its sixteenth volume, an extraordinary achievement considering the Munich label Compost Records’ founder and compiler Michael Reinboth pretty much unveiled the term ‘future jazz’. This epic series of jazz-meets-electronica compilations began in 1995 and I’ve been a fan since the first edition when Michael drew the dots between artists as diverse as Luke Vibert, Patrick Pulsinger, Jimi Tenor and The Mighty Bop (alongside some lesser known names). A sonic space of jazz-infused house, breakbeats, future jazz and spaced out electronic oddities, the shared aesthetic was a jazz sensibility even if the music lived in other generic boxes. Not in a jazz sense of live improvisational musicianship but certainly in the sense of freedom, vibes, experimentation. From this early outing the world has caught up with Michael’s vision, a vision in turn inspired by Detroit’s own ‘Hi-Tech Jazz’, the Underground Resistance (Galaxy 2 Galaxy) all-time classic that revealed that jazz and electronic music could thrive together.Thirty one years after kickstarting this journey, the label returns with volume 16 and it’s another Michael (Rütten) who has been invited by his old friend to co-curate, and together they've absolutely smashed it, offering possibly my favourite volume so far with a roster that includes Momoko Gill, Trinidadian Deep, Felix Laband, Emanative & Jessica Lauren and DJ Oil.Michael Rütten is himself an essential cog in spreading the gospel about future-leaning jazz, electronic music and more. His globally-syndicated Soulsearching radio show has run for decades, he’s a music journalist, DJ and producer and has promoted key independent artists in his hometown of Frankfurt. Who better to join in the dig?I asked them a few questions on the eve of the release.. Michael Reinboth JT - Firstly, thank you for such a great compilation! Is it the best one yet? For my tastes it definitely is.Michael Reinboth - Many thanks for the compliments. Michael Rütten - Wow, that‘s a great compliment, thank you!JT - You’ve both been friends for so long and you’ve both curated many compilations but is this the first time you have compiled a record together?Michael Reinboth - Yes indeed, we’ve known each other since the beginning of Compost, and have a a genuine shared sense of taste, a journey through time.  After Vol. 15, I had a few good tracks up my sleeve but somehow not enough to fill a 3-LP / 2-CD set. That’s when Michael Rütten came along at just the right time. He had so many great suggestions that I was quite—and extremely—positively surprised, and I motivated myself to go into seclusion once again. Ha, I then found some rough FSOJ track listings on my old computer, gave them another listen, and sent my (old) ideas to Michael. Well, Michael Rütten really stepped up his game, so we currently have over 50 great tracks on our list and are already planning the next Vol. 17 for 2027.And we've decided to go on tour together and play this music in clubs, that is, to DJ. It's been a while since we've done that, and we think it's about time. Well, we're pretty good at it. After all, we have 40 years of experience.Michael Rütten - Yeah, and it happened almost by coincidence as we were talking on the phone earlier this year about potential compilations on Compost Records in the near future generally. I was relistening to some of the last ‘Future Sounds Of Jazz’ editions, especially Vol. 13 which Michael compiled on his own, for me one of the best ones, speaking about the selection, the flow, the feeling. All making sense. Also, I am thinking about a follow up of  ‘Soulsearching’ as it’s been quite a while. We speak on a regular basis about music, life, and what’s going on in the world of music and Compost Records. A new chapter of ‘Future Sounds Of Jazz’ has been ‘in the air’ since a couple of years, as not only there are so many new brilliant artists and tracks floating around that match with the idea of the series but also a new generation of young people discovering and appreciating this special sound of no boundaries, an open minded blend of jazz and electronics. I do feel and recognize this through my radio shows and DJ sets. So, as Michael mentioned that he could only think of two people - apart from himself - who could compile a FSOJ - one of them was me - we quite spontaneously decided to do the next edition together. Overnight we had a list of more than 50 tracks and started to sort (them) out. Which has been great fun! And apart from our dear friendship and shared love for good music I really do appreciate Michael’s attitude of ‘let’s do this’ and his open mind. And trust. As I do like his way of DJing ever since. Happy that someone just recently described us as pioneers of the DJ culture, instead of speaking of veterans ; ) We are still doing it out of pure passion. Neverending. So I am very much looking forward to travelling and sharing the decks again with Michael, spreading the music we love. Making people dance to timeless tunes of past, present, future via quite spontaneous DJ sets. No prepared set lists, always inspiring, always great fun also! JT - How did you approach the shared responsibility? Were there tracks that you had to fight over to be included or was it a relaxed process? Did you have fun?Michael Reinboth - First of all, it was a pleasure to hear each other's suggestions, it's always enriching. Then we basically gave the tracks grades, on a scale of one to three. No arguments at all. We were pretty much in complete agreement.Michael Rütten - Exciting, relaxed, open minded. Always enriching to hear each other’s new discoveries. And rediscoveries, tunes, that go a long way back and feel just right in the here and now. As we are both connected with so many artists of different genres from around the world who sent their music in and checking what’s going on daily or even 24/7 ... we both can’t just listen to everything. But tell each other about exciting new stuff. And I think it‘s a premiere that a fully analogue recorded jazz song made it onto Future Sounds Of Jazz - Brittany Davis’ ‘Sun & Moon’. Thanks to Michael’s open minded flexibility he instantly said yes to my idea. Oh, and no fights, never. FUN! JT - When you started out with the idea of ‘Future Jazz’ 31 years ago (!), there were a lot less artists operating in that way but there seems to be a galaxy full of them now. Compost and the Future Jazz compilations have undoubtedly been leaders in the development and widespread awareness of the ‘scene’ - do you recognise that yourself and have a sense of pride in your essential contribution?Michael Reinboth - The term “Future Jazz” didn’t exist in 1994 (neither as a genre nor as a catchphrase among DJs), but I wanted to give this new stylistic phenomenon a powerful (and provocative) name. Basically, it meant: this isn’t acid jazz (i.e. old stuff or old stuff played anew) but electronically produced music, mostly created by recluses in the studio, as opposed to live bands. To answer your question about whether I have a sense of pride: yes, at the very least I can claim that, with the FSOJ series, I helped found and shape this genre.JT - You have both been at the forefront of exploring and revealing the links between electronic music and jazz for decades. What has changed in your opinion? Michael Reinboth - Back then, as mentioned above, it was mostly individuals producing jazzy electronic music; today, there are far more collectives (perhaps the first being Jazzanova) that can also perform it live (the Cinematic Orchestra, for example). It always takes time (much longer for jazz than for techno) for the tracks to become more complex and sophisticated - that is, to delve deeper into the essence of jazz, discover something new, and master electronic equipment and production techniques at the same level. But there were phases when Future Jazz was flooded by Neo Disco, New Wave revivals, Trap, Lo-Fi, and Broken Techno. That was also one reason why the intervals between FSOJ events grew longer. At this point, I have to once again give a big shout-out to Michael Rütten, who really helped me get back on track with it.Michael Rütten - Many projects, bands and producers that combine both worlds (jazz and electronics) have appeared on the scene over the last 10-15 years. Probably a lot of them inspired by the likes of Jason Swinscoe‘s Cinematic Orchestra, Theo Parrish, Nicolas Jaar, Matthew Herbert, just to name a few. Contrast Trio out of Frankfurt is one of them, just re-united with a new approach, or Momoko Gill out of London, who combines classic songwriting and live played drums by herself with jazz, soul and electronic elements. Emanative aka Nick Woodmansey also produces and plays music with the live aspect in mind from scratch. DJ Oil from Marseille/Paris with his quite unique sound. So much has happened and is still happening on the forefront of music which sits somewhere in between genres. I think that the pandemic has also played a huge role regarding this point. Artists had to find a new way of expression and took the time to either re-invent themselves or/and explore new territories. Jazz is the teacher, always or let‘s say again. JT - There’s a deep and hypnotic aesthetic running throughout the compilation (with a few exceptions). This cosmic-ambient-krauty-repetition way of composition is something I’ve noticed myself a lot recently on labels like We Jazz, International Anthem and many others. Do you think that this is the natural result of a generation of jazz (and jazz-curious) musicians growing up knowing and understanding electronic music? Is it also a sign of the times? A human need to explore slowness and transcendence in an ever-crazier world?Michael Reinboth - Oh yes, I do think that slowing down and a certain catharsis - escaping this crazy world - is a reason to turn to this music more than ever. It helps; it heals a little.Michael Rütten - Well, that is something I’ve just realized while doing the tracklist for the CD/digital release of FSOJ 16! And yes, it‘s definitely a sign of the times we are living in. And also all things go round in circles. With the overload of overproduced music plus AI most recently, producers, musicians and people feel the need to slow down, dive into soul-soothing repetitive moments, going back to the roots actually. Be it via ancient rhythms, ambient (healing) sounds, it’s soulsearching in the end. Seeking warmth and something to hold on to in this mad world. Electronic music evolved out of repetitive elements, exploring of sounds and a very free approach, far from limiting forms of music theory. Bringing the human aspect more into the creation. It’s a very exciting time period right now! JT - It’s been four years since the last Future Jazz compilation which had quite a different feel to this new one - What do you see NOW that could be a new direction in another four years in the future?Michael Reinboth - It’s completely trend-independent, but Michael and I have a few older tracks with a disco vibe—disco jazz, so to speak. Let’s see if we can put together a ‘Future Sounds of Disco Jazz’ compilation with them. For Vol. 19 or 20, I could imagine something more hardcore tech-jazz.I’m curious to see how our Future Sounds of Jazz DJ gigs go. The sound has been totally underground for years and I hope that will change in four years. We’re working on it.  Michael Rütten - Like Michael Reinboth said: trend-independent is the word here. Timelessness, always forward thinking without following any trends. Just following our instinct, gut and feeling. BUY HERE! https://compostrecords.bandcamp.com/album/future-sounds-of-jazz-vol-16
items._cn_summary: 本文围绕慕尼黑厂牌Compost Records旗下《Future Sounds of Jazz》系列第十六卷展开，采访了该系列创始人Michael Reinboth与共同策划者Michael Rütten。该合辑延续了自1995年以来的核心理念——将爵士精神与电子舞曲、碎拍、未来爵士融合，以自由度与实验性取代传统即兴演奏观念。第十六卷曲目包括Momoko Gill、Trinidadian Deep、Felix Laband、Emanative与Jessica Lauren等艺术家，选曲跨越爵士氛围、灵魂乐与电子律动。两位策划人以多年合作与全球电台节目经验为背景，呈现出一张跨越流派的选辑。内容为采访形式而非深入乐评，信息量有限但展现了欧洲独立厂牌对爵士与电子融合美学的持续探索。

items.body: Cold Spring hosts a label night at The Globe in Glossop on 3 October 2026, with T.A.G.C., Satori, Colossloth and Llyn Y Cwn performing alongside a Cold Spring stall. Doors run from 7pm to 10:30pm, with tickets available through Resident Advisor and the event’s Facebook page. T.A.G.C. (The Anti Group Communications) was devised by Adi Newton and Steven James Turner in 1978 as a multi-dimensional research and development project. Newton uses T.A.G.C. as an outlet for his research into psycho-acoustic music, built from carefully constructed aural rituals. He is also the driving force behind Clock DVA, The Anti Group and The Future, the pre-Human League project, and a key figure in the development of electronic, industrial and experimental music since the late 1970s. T.A.G.C.’s “Iso-Erotic Calibration” is out now on Cold Spring on CD, LP and limited LP. British industrial veterans Satori formed in 1984 and have released material on cult labels including Broken Flag, Mindscan, Cold Spring and Tesco Organisation. The Glossop date doubles as the launch for Satori’s new album, “Your Life Is Worth Nothing,” which pairs harsh noise and power electronics with heavier percussive beats than the act’s earlier material. Colossloth, from the Midlands, marks 20 years as a project in 2026 and launches the new album “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites” at the Glossop show. Colossloth’s music moves between brooding, abrasive passages and more transcendental material, drawing on industrial, ethnic tribalism and rave influences. Llyn Y Cwn is the solo project of Ben Powell, who has made electronic music for over 25 years, drawing on the landscapes of North Wales and his experience on Arctic research cruises. He presents “Megaliths In Dub” versus “Aniara” as an exclusive first listen at the Glossop show. About Cold Spring Cold Spring is a British independent record label focused on industrial, power electronics, noise, dark ambient and experimental music. The label has released material from artists including T.A.G.C., Satori and Colossloth, and has previously staged label nights and compilations such as the “Arise – A Cold Spring Sampler” collection. The Glossop show brings together acts from across the label’s roster, including two new album launches from Satori and Colossloth, alongside a live set from Clock DVA and Human League co-founder Adi Newton under his T.A.G.C. name.

items.body: Black Lotus, the project of artist Thai, is releasing a concept EP titled “In a Room Full of Dreams” through dark synthwave, dark synth-pop, darkwave and related electronic sounds built around synesthesia, dreams, memory and perception. The title track arrives on 14 September 2026. A streaming link for the title track itself was not confirmed at the time of writing. The EP follows the earlier single “Dreams of Snakes“, already available on Spotify, and includes the tracks “When Sound Becomes Colour” and “Synthesia” alongside the title track. Geert Coppens joins Black Lotus on ‘Dreams of Snakes’ Belgian musician Geert Coppens performs as a vocal duo with Thai on “Dreams of Snakes” and has also contributed to the EP’s visual and video work. Coppens’ back-catalogue reaches into Belgium’s early minimal wave, darkwave and coldwave scenes. About Black Lotus and Geert Coppens Geert Coppens is a Belgian musician who co-founded the Micrart Group with classmate Peter Bonne in 1977, and the two went on to form the new wave band Autumn, active from 1980 to 1984. In 1982, while still working within Autumn, Coppens and Bonne began Twilight Ritual as a side project exploring a darker, more minimal sound; the pair kept Twilight Ritual a two-person project until their paths split in 1985, when Bonne went on to form A Split Second with Marc Ickx while Coppens continued designing artwork for that project and kept working under the Micrart banner. Autumn material was later compiled by Minimal Wave Records on the “Synthesize” collection, and Twilight Ritual has since been reissued on Genetic Music, Onderstroom Records and Wave Records, whose 2021 compilation “1982-2021” gathered 34 tracks spanning the project’s full history. Coppens has also worked more recently under the name Das Cabinett and, in 2023, teamed with Miami-based artist Nina Belief on the EP “In Memory Of” as Faceless 50. His appearance on “Dreams of Snakes” extends that history of collaboration into Black Lotus’s “In a Room Full of Dreams”. Black Lotus is the project of artist Thai, working across music, dance, photography, video, installation and performance-based visual art. “In a Room Full of Dreams” continues that multidisciplinary approach, pairing the EP’s concept around synesthesia and altered perception with Coppens’ contributions to both the music and the accompanying visuals.

items._cn_summary: Black Lotus（艺术家Thai的项目）将发行概念EP《In a Room Full of Dreams》，围绕联觉、梦境、记忆与感知主题展开。EP包含四首曲目，涵盖从前期单曲《Dreams of Snakes》到标题曲及《When Sound Becomes Colour》《Synthesia》等作品，风格定位于暗潮合成波、暗潮合成流行及相关电子声响。比利时音乐人Geert Coppens作为客座人声搭档参与《Dreams of Snakes》，并为EP提供视觉与影像创作。Coppens自1977年起深耕比利时极简浪潮、暗潮与冷潮领域，曾与Peter Bonne共同组建Autumn与Twilight Ritual，作品经Minimal Wave Records、Onderstroom Records等地下厂牌再版发行。Black Lotus本身横跨音乐、舞蹈、摄影、录像、装置与行为艺术，此次EP延续多学科路径，将音乐概念与视觉呈现紧密结合，整体呈现介于复古暗潮语汇与当代跨媒介实验之间的制作思路。

items.body: 東京都交響楽団第1049回定期演奏会Aシリーズ Tokyo Metropolitan Symphony Orchestra Subscription Concert No.1049 A Series 2026年8月8日 東京芸術劇場 2026/8/8 Tokyo Metropolitan Theatre Reviewed by 齋藤俊夫(Toshio Saito) Photos by (c)Rikimaru Hotta／提供：東京都交響楽団 <演奏> 指揮：尾高忠明 ピアノ：北村朋幹(*) コンサートマスター：山本友重 東京都交響楽団 <曲目> 三善晃：オーケストラのための『ノエシス』 松村禎三：『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』(*) エルガー：『エニグマ変奏曲』   “無”と書いた軸を掛けても、何もなくなりません。“死”と書いた軸の場合は、何もかもなくなる。“無”ではなくならん。“死”ではなくなる！ 井上靖『本覺坊遺文』より 本公演の前半2曲、三善晃『ノエシス』と松村禎三『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』に深く刻み込まれているのは、人間がそこから逃れることのできない「死」という事象であった。 6分ほどのごく短い作品ながら、三善の音楽の全ての要素が含まれていると言っても過言ではない『ノエシス』の、雷神か怨霊が乱れ狂い歌い狂うような音響に続く後奏の静けさ。その静けさを構成するのは、「死」だ。いや、乱れ歌う音響もまた「死」の体験を延長したものなのかもしれない。なんと苛烈な世界で三善は生きてきたのか。苛烈な世界で「死」を忘れることなく想いつつ、生き抜いた彼の美的倫理……ああ、過酷だ。あまりにも過酷すぎる。 松村禎三『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』、これもまた苛烈な音楽であった。松村の原体験に結核での長い療養生活があることは周知の事実だが、その生と死が紙一重となった体験を「凝視すること」を音楽体験に変換した「オスティナート（執拗な反復）」の楽想の恐ろしさ。師・伊福部昭の、生を肯定するたくましいオスティナートとは全く異なる、ひたすら「死とは何か」を念じ続ける強迫的なオスティナート。第1楽章序盤から結末まで、北村朋幹の澄み切ったピアノの音色が音楽に透徹した思索性を与え、またそのピアノを起点としてのオーケストラの響きを捌き切る尾高の指揮、それに応える都響の演奏、どこにも隙がない。隙がないということは松村オスティナートの強迫的音響が終始こちらの心の芯に刺さり、震わせ続けるということだ。なんたる音楽体験。 第2楽章に入り、冒頭からの静かな北村のピアノ独奏が厳しく、されど儚く、でも死を凝視する強い意志をもって。諸行無常という諦観とは無縁な、もっと力強い音楽。やがて始まるピアノのトレモロに生命力が宿り、そこからオーケストラとピアノの強靭な楽想が噴火する。これは生への意志か？ 死への意志か？ 全てをねじ伏せるような力強さ。だが最後（最期）は静寂の中へ、死へと落ちゆく。全てはそこに帰す、という厳然たる真実をこちらに突きつけて、終わる。 公演後半は、人類が2つの世界大戦を経験する以前のいわゆる「クラシック音楽」であるエルガー『エニグマ変奏曲』の美しさを、エルガーの世界的権威尾高忠明の指揮で聴くというなんとも贅沢なプログラムであった。 最初に憂いを帯びた主題が提示される時点で「あー、クラシック音楽は綺麗だ」とうっとりとさせられる。そこから典雅な第1変奏、無窮動的第2変奏、おどけた第3変奏……と進むそれぞれの音楽が実に「これでしかありえない」という確固たる構築性を持って組み立てられている。ヨーロッパの教会建築のような堂々たる荘厳かつ崇高な音楽が現前し、そこに筆者は音楽の持つ陽性な宗教的精神すら汲み取った。さらに、建築といってもガチガチに表面なや内部が固まることなく、生物的な柔軟さとしなやかさをも兼ね備えた有機的建築物である。第9変奏「ニムロッド」の優しく温かい音楽や、最終第14変奏の即興的ダイナミズムを持ちつつ完璧な構造を現実化したレアリゼなど、まさに尾高の独壇場ではないか。なんというか、「さすが世界レベルの権威だ」とぐうの音も出ないほどに心服させられた。 死を強く思わせる前半、優しく抱きしめてくれる後半、と対照的な音楽ながら、どちらも超一流の仕事を聴かせてもらった。尾高マエストロ、北村朋幹、都響、皆に心からの賛辞を。 (2026/9/15)
items._cn_summary: 本场音乐会以「生与死」为核心概念串联三首作品。前半场聚焦日本当代作曲：三善晃《诺埃西斯》以短暂而密集的音响呈现雷神般的狂乱与死寂交织，松村禎三《第二钢琴协奏曲》以伊福部昭门下的强逼性固定低音乐思，将结核病疗养经历中对生死的凝视转化为钢琴与管弦乐的对峙；北村朋幹的钢琴音色澄澈，尾高忠明指挥下的都響配合严密。后半场回归欧洲传统，以埃尔加《谜语变奏曲》的典雅建筑性结构与温暖主题收束全晚。前后两半在生死主题上构成强烈对照，演出水准受到高度评价，评论融入了文学引用与哲学思考。

items.body: 〈過剰〉を〈過剰〉のままで―沖澤のどか／SKOの《トゥランガリーラ交響曲》｜内野 儀 Excess in All Its Excess: Nodoka Okisawa and the SKO’s Turangalîla-Symphonie 2026年8月23日 キッセイ文化ホール（長野県松本文化会館） セイジ・オザワ 松本フェスティバル オーケストラ コンサート Aプログラム（2日目） 2026/8/23 Kissei Culture Hall (Nagano Prefecture Matsumoto Culture Hall) 2026 Seiji Ozawa Matsumoto Festival: Orchestral Concert — Program A (Day 2) Reviewed by 内野 儀(UCHINO, Tadashi) Photos by 山田毅(Takeshi Yamada)／2026OMF :大窪道治 （Michiharu Okubo）／2026OMF 〈演奏〉 指揮：沖澤のどか ピアノ：務川慧悟 オンド・マルトノ：原田節 管弦楽：サイトウ・キネン・オーケストラ 〈曲目〉 オリヴィエ・メシアン《トゥランガリーラ交響曲》 ©山田毅／2026OMF 《トゥランガリーラ交響曲》は、あらゆる意味で〈過剰〉な作品である。85分、10楽章、100人を超える大編成オーケストラ。独奏ピアノとオンド・マルトノ、数多くの打楽器奏者、そしてピアノ・チェレスタ・鍵盤グロッケンシュピール・ヴィブラフォンからなる「ガムラン」群。ティンパニもハープもない代わりに、これだけのものが投入されている。 〈過剰〉は規模にとどまらない。メシアン自身、第1楽章の中間部を「ポリリズム、ポリモダリティ、ポリミュージック」と呼んだ(1)第4楽章の再現部については、スケルツォ主題、ピアノ独奏、コントラバスのピツィカート、ガムラン群、リズム・ペダルを奏するウッドブロック、小トルコ・シンバル、小太鼓のリズム、木管とホルンの第1トリオ、弦の第2トリオ、そしてトロンボーンの第一循環主題（〈彫像の主題〉）——10の独立した音楽が同時に鳴ると自ら数え上げている（Messiaen, p. 227; Shenton, p. 49）。したがって、打楽器奏者には「第六感」をもちあわせた第一級の精度が必要で、小さな誤りひとつで音楽が壊れる、と書き残している（p.156; p.15）。 メシアンはまた、「歓びの讃歌(hymn to joy)」と本作を形容するが、その「歓び」の定義そのものが〈過剰〉である。「17世紀の実直なブルジョワ市民が味わうような穏やかで満ち足りた歓びではない」と否定形からその定義を始め、「不幸のただなかにあってかろうじて垣間見た者だけが思い描きうるもの、超人的で、溢れ出し、目を眩ませ、過剰なものだ」と書く（p.151; p.6）。「愛」についても、「トリスタンとイゾルデの媚薬によって象徴されるような、すべてを超え、自らの外にあるすべてを消し去る宿命的で抗いがたい愛」であるとする（同上）。この「愛」が、媚薬による絶対的／超越的「愛」である以上、そこに暴力性が畳み込まれているのは当然である。実際、冒頭でトロンボーンが重い3度で叩きつける第一循環主題を、メシアンは〈彫像の主題〉と呼び、メキシコの記念建造物の恐るべき残酷さを喚起するものと説明している(2)。要するに、この作品において〈過剰〉は方法や結果ではない。〈過剰〉こそが主題である。 そのことを考えるとき、私はどうしても作曲年代のことを思う。1945年6月25日、セルゲイ・クーセヴィツキーがメシアンに委嘱状を書いた。ドイツ降伏の7週間後である。メシアンの返信は8月20日、《ハラウィ(Harawi)》を書き上げつつあったプティシェ(Petichet)のサマーホームからで、「美しく、相応の規模をもった作品を書きたい。そのためには夢み、愛し、練り上げ、急がずに管弦楽化する時間が要る」だった(3)。 ソプラノとピアノのための連作歌曲《ハラウィ》(1945）、この《トゥランガリーラ交響曲》（1946–48）、無伴奏12声のための《5つのルシャン》（1948）。のちにトリスタン三部作と呼ばれる三作は、この数年のうちに続けて書かれた。編成も規模もまったく異なるが、いずれも愛と死をめぐる同じ主題系のもとにある。メシアンの作品のなかで、カトリック信仰を直接の主題としない数少ない例でもある。 同じ1945年の秋、メシアンにはもうひとつ差し迫った委嘱があった。アンリ・バロー(Henry Barraud)からの、戦時中の強制移送者を追悼する作品である。11月2日の演奏会に向けて、9月22日——《ハラウィ)》完成の1週間後——に楽譜を渡せるように《強制移送者たちの歌（Chant des déportés）》を書き、さらに、10月10日の日記には、「クーセヴィツキーのために交響的作品を書く」と記している(4)。 戦時中の強制移送者を追悼する作品と、この巨大な交響曲の初期的構想とは、同じ数週間のなかにあった。作曲そのものは1946年7月17日から1948年11月29日まで(p.151; p.4)行われたが、作曲者自身についても、よく知られているように、自らが収監されていたゲルリッツの捕虜収容所で《世の終わりのための四重奏曲》を1941年に書いて演奏もしている(5)。 1945年5月16日——ドイツ降伏の8日後——にメシアンが雑誌『ヴォロンテ(Volontés)』へ寄せた文章がある。「現代音楽には乾いた非人間的なものが多すぎる！」とかれは書く。「来たるべき革新者は言語だけの革命家であってはならない。絶望の塊や、人の住まない惑星ではなく、大文字の愛を」。そして、待ち望まれている「解放者」、すなわち「愛の作曲家」の到来をともに祈ってくれと呼びかけている(6)。「絶望の塊」。「人の住まない惑星」。「解放者」。1945年5月のヨーロッパで書かれた語彙である。 この交響曲が戦争を描いていると言いたいのではない。標題にも、作曲者の膨大な自己解説のどこにも、そんなことは書かれていない。だが、これほどの規模の肯定が何に対する応答だったのかを問わずに済ませることもできないのではないか。「不幸のただなかで垣間見た者だけが思い描きうる歓び」——この条件節に、1946年のヨーロッパで指示対象がなかったとは、私には考えにくい。廃墟の記憶は、フランスが戦勝国であったからといって消えるようなものではない。 専門家ではないので見落としが多いことだろうが、短期間ではあるものの目を通すことができた英語文献にかぎると、メシアンと戦争をめぐる議論は《四重奏曲》と占領期に集中しているようで、トリスタン三部作のほうは、もっぱら二つの方向に読まれてきた印象が残る。ひとつは本作についてのシュルレアリスム的プログラムの解読、もうひとつは作曲者の私生活——病んでゆく最初の妻クレール・デルボスと、イヴォンヌ・ロリオとの関係——への還元である。 後者は、私にはあまり実りがあるとは思えない。第一に、メシアン自身が私生活と作品を明示的に結びつけていない。シェントンも、まさにその理由でその論点を扱わないと断っている(7)。第二に、そもそも個人的な恋愛の高揚だけでは、この規模と構造を説明しきれない。この規模は、私的な感情の器としては明らかに大きすぎる。 もちろん、〈過剰〉は、説明されるべき欠陥ではない。これは端的に誇大妄想である。あるいは、過大妄想とでもいうべきか。初演前のNBCの放送でクーセヴィツキーは、《春の祭典》に次ぐ今世紀最大の作品だと言い切った(8)。誇大／過大な言い方である。だが誇大／過大であることこそが、この作品の内容なのだと思う。廃墟のあとに、この規模で〈愛〉と〈歓び〉を主張すること。〈まっとう〉な振る舞いではない。そして、〈まっとう〉ではないことが必要だったのではないか。 メシアンは1953年、自分は神秘主義の音楽家ではなくシュルレアリストの音楽家である、ただしその超現実への欲望は超自然によって超えられている、と述べている(9)。シェントンはこの発言を、ブルトンの『シュルレアリスム第二宣言』（1930）に重ねている。ブルトンがそこで求めたのは、「生と死、現実と想像、過去と未来、伝達可能性と伝達不可能性、高と低がもはや矛盾として知覚されなくなるような精神の一点」(10)であった。第一次大戦後に成立したシュルレアリスムの論理が、戦後期のメシアンの自己規定に重ねられる。歓びと恐怖を対立させないこと、〈愛の主題〉と〈彫像の主題〉とを同じ作品に置くこと。それは意匠ではなく、あの時代への応答となる思想として、私には聴こえる。 だから、この作品を単一の陶酔へ向かって収束させる聴き方には、私は与しない。緩徐楽章の〈愛の主題〉に匂い立つような官能を求め、終曲に忘我を求める——そうした期待は、作品の多層性を単一の陶酔へ狭める読みだと思う。 サンスクリットの題、ヒンドゥーのターラ、ガムラン、メキシコの記念建造物、ボスとシャガールとピラネージ。快楽の園と出口のない牢獄。この作品が抱え込んでいるものは、どこまでも多元的であり、その多元性には〈地獄的なもの〉まで含まれている。二元論を拒むこと、一つの中心へ回収されないこと。それが、この〈過剰〉の設計思想である。 ©大窪道治／2026OMF 23日の演奏は、まさにそれを鳴らした。沖澤のどかはこの日、指揮棒を持たずに振った。打点を棒で叩き込まない身ぶりが奏者に過剰な圧をかけず、テンポは「押される」のではなく「走り出す」。第5楽章や終曲の疾走感は、絶対的なテンポの速さからではなく、その場その場の奏者との呼吸から生まれてくる。〈自然体〉、という言い方がふさわしい。 そしてこの〈自然体〉は、〈過剰〉を手なずけるための方便ではなかった。同時多発は同時多発のまま残り、しかしカオスにはならない。第2楽章冒頭で三つの群が別々のリズムを刻む箇所も、ガムラン群が主要主題と併走する箇所も、均されることなく、それぞれの層として聴こえてくる。沖澤は公演前に、「すべてをクリアにすることによって濃厚にしたい」と語っていた。「どこまでも緻密に作ったうえで、それを体に沁み込ませる。そして、オーケストラが曲を知り尽くした状態にしたうえで本番に自由になるような——そこを目指」す、とも(11)。明晰さは削減ではない。〈過剰〉が混濁ではなく〈過剰〉として聴こえるための、重要な条件の一つである。抑制でも整理でもなく、〈過剰〉を〈過剰〉のまま、リアルタイムに立ち上げること。この作品にこれほど相応しい方法があるだろうか。 その姿勢が最も明瞭に出たのが、第8楽章の終わりである。「愛の展開」と題されたこの楽章では、〈和音の主題〉がよく聞こえる。だがこの楽章は〈彫像の主題〉で閉じられる。しかもその最後の音は、管楽器から、タムタム、大太鼓、ピアノ、コントラバスへと受け渡される。打たれた瞬間から消えはじめる音である。「愛の展開」が行き着いた先に、この落下がある。減衰を聴きつづけるあいだ、それが恐ろしいのか美しいのかは判別できない。沖澤はその減衰を、かなりの長さにわたって聴かせた。急ぐ理由がないから急がない。それだけのことが、この作品ではほとんど過激に響く。他方、全曲を締める終曲の最後は、極端に引き延ばされることなく、比較的速いポイントですっきりと切り上げられた。 四つの循環主題のうち、メシアンが唯一象徴的意味を与えなかったのが〈和音の主題〉である。かれはこれを、主題というよりも異なる音の層を成り立たせるための口実だと言い、中世錬金術の標語を引いている——分離し、そして凝固させよ。要素へと分解し、新たな形へ組み直す(12)。この日の演奏が全曲にわたっておこなっていたのは、まさにその作業だった。 ©山田毅／2026OMF 務川慧悟のピアノは、第1楽章のカデンツァから第5楽章の強打まで、和音の一音一音が分離して聴こえる明晰さを保った。強奏でも音が濁らない。舞台前方下手側にピアノ、チェレスタ、鍵盤グロッケンシュピール、ヴィブラフォン、上手側にオンド・マルトノという配置で、鍵盤・打楽器群の合奏はきわめて緊密だった。原田節のオンド・マルトノは、前から13列目やや下手寄りという私の席では音量的に前に出てこず、弦との溶け合いのなかに沈む場面が多かった。席位置による部分が大きいだろう。 緩急の振幅も、極大から極小まで振り切ったダイナミクスの幅も、「楽譜どおり」と言ってしまえばそれまでかもしれない。だが今回聴こえたのは、楽譜の指示の「再現」ではなく「現実化」だった。書かれていることが、その場で実際に起きるのだ。 私には、廃墟の記憶のうえに立つ〈まっとう〉ではない規模の肯定として聴こえた。それは一つの答えに収束することを拒み、多元的なまま、〈過剰〉なまま鳴りつづけるように感じられた。きな臭さを増していく2026年の日本で、その〈過剰〉が整理も馴致もされずに響いたことには、意味があると思う。純粋な音楽として、である。 （2026/9/15) 註 (1)Messiaen, O. items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评围绕冲澤のどか指挥的梅西安《图伦加利拉交响曲》演出展开，从「过度」这一概念切入，梳理了作品的规模、节奏复杂性以及梅西安本人对「喜悦」与「爱」的极端定义。乐评将作品放置在1945年战后欧洲的历史语境中，探讨这部庞大肯定性作品与战争记忆之间的潜在关联，质疑以往将该作仅归入超现实主义程式或作曲家私生活解读的倾向。文字以学术分析为主，引证作曲家书信、日记及英文学术文献，结构严谨但偏向音乐学研究而非纯粹聆听体验描述。

items._cn_summary: Will Long 的《Long Trax 5》延续其生命周期系列第5作，以「反AI」为创作宣言，所有音色均通过钢琴、合成器与节奏机等硬件设备完成，刻意回避软件与算法介入。专辑收录六首长篇house曲目，在极简框架中展开：电子音色经过大幅削减后形成无机质感，底层却透出有机的柔韧与温度，这种矛盾的张力贯穿整体。整体氛围偏梦幻、内省，强调听后残留的余韵而非舞曲律动的即时冲击。制作理念本身带有对当下AI生成音乐趋势的抵抗立场，声音选择与处理方式也呼应这一主题。作为实验性house作品，专辑的硬件纯化思路与氛围house的美学契合，但在实验深度上仍偏向氛围延伸而非结构革新。

items._cn_summary: 这是WILLOW第八张专辑，相较前作独奏式制作，本作转为乐队编制并由长期合作者Chris Greatti全面参与制作，日裔歌手Mei Simmons受邀客串。专辑以先锋爵士摇滚为骨架，强调自由展开的实验精神与艺术性表达，兼具灵性色彩。乐队形态的转变让作品呈现出比前作更丰富的层次感和即兴张力，融合了爵士的自由流动与摇滚的粗粝质感，是一张在结构上更具野心、在声音探索上更为大胆的作品。

items.body: Tracing lines of loss, the flaws of being human, and aspects of love, solitude, and isolation, Shade is the twelfth full-length record from Grouper, a continuation of ambient reflection and introspection. The songs of Pacific Northwest artist Liz Harris absorb their surroundings, including the deep mists of the Bay Area, which echo on through the use of wet reverb and the slight decay which eats away at the tone like a heart slowly shattering; a slight erosion takes place, in the heart and in the music, a dampening caused by incessant rainfall. Shade is a collection of songs which span roughly fifteen years. Harris calls it ‘an album about respite, and the coast, poetically and literally… how we frame ourselves in a landscape, how in turn it frames ourselves; memories and experiences carried forward mapping our connection to place.’ Sections of Shade were recorded on California’s Mount Tamalpais, during a residency many years ago. Other songs were recorded in Portland and stretch back even further, while the rest of the music was recorded more recently in Astoria. Cohesive and thoughtful, the music has a strong spine, even while appearing tonally fragile. Subject to maritime storms, rolling banks of fog, and the unpredictability of its running rivers, which can either sail along or surge with a sudden, unstoppable force, Grouper’s music nevertheless offers a placid and forever-calm space. Opening song ‘Followed The Ocean’ has that classic Grouper sound – hazy harmonies hovering in the murk, her voice floating, apparition-like, somewhere nearby and yet lost in the distance, achingly close to home but remaining forever cut off from someone; lost to the waters, even though the shoreline is in sight. The slower pace allows for a more thoughtful sound, as if she’s processing things along with the listeners, working things out with the help of the music. Other songs feature a clearer sound, as the guitar provides the rhythm, the accompaniment, and a slower, more reclined tempo. The finger-plucked melody of ‘Ode to the Blue’ offers more of a delicate and comforting sound, as if the instrument understands. And it does. The guitar offers solace and protects its companion after experiencing a life-altering loss. Even the vocals seem tired, diminished to humming a frail melody and ending in a sigh. Eventually, it finds rest. As always, the music is exceptionally beautiful. The murky, sunken tones only add to the depth of the music and the atmosphere is composed and relaxed at all times. Maybe it’s the location; it definitely has an effect on the music, the natural environment adding so much more to the music than a pedal chain or the use of new equipment. ‘The Way Her Hair Falls’ is a mesmerising song, with a gentleness that only Grouper can usher out, while ‘Kelso (Blue Sky)’ is a beautiful and bittersweet ending that begins optimistically and ends in heartbreak. Harris has produced another stellar record with this release. Shade is out on Kranky on October 22. Shade by Grouper www.grouper.bandcamp.com

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑横跨约十五年的创作时间，录制地点散布于加州Mount Tamalpais、波特兰以及阿斯托里亚，地理环境深刻渗透进声音肌理。Liz Harris以湿润混响与缓慢衰减塑造出潮湿、朦胧的音景，吉他与模糊人声在雾气中漂浮、时隐时现，营造出距离感与亲密感并存的氛围。整张作品节奏缓慢，旋律如指弹吉他的细腻拨弦和疲惫的哼唱般克制内敛，主题围绕失去、孤独、记忆与地方归属展开。音乐看似音调脆弱，却拥有内在的结构支撑，海岸、雾气、雨水等自然意象被转化为可听的声音质感，呈现出沉思与安抚交织的聆听体验。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items._cn_summary: 这是挪威二人组Sudan Dudan的第五张专辑，延续了他们二十年来的传统北欧民谣路线。专辑以原声吉他为主导，辅以挪威传统乐器如小提琴、langeleik（挪威筝）、里拉琴和口弦。整体氛围带有忧郁反思色彩，歌词涉及大地、星辰、神话与失落等人文主题，以挪威语演唱。专辑中穿插了几首特色曲目：一首重新演绎并改编自某首法国旋律的轻快作品，以及一首采用挪威传统tralling无词人声技法的曲目。终曲罕见地引入了电吉他，深沉twang音色为专辑增添了独特的收尾。制作精良，编曲富有想象力，作为传统挪威民谣在当代语境下的呈现值得聆听。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了圣多美和普林西比两个小岛在七十至八十年代录制的Puxa音乐。Puxa是一种混合多种非洲前葡萄牙殖民地节奏的复合舞曲，融合了merengue、Kompas、Soukouss和Benga等元素，乐评强调其能召唤精灵或驱赶恶魔的仪式性功能。乐评指出，虽然岛屿人口稀少且录音条件有限，但音乐呈现出远超预期的丰富层次：多把吉他交织盘旋、主唱与和声此起彼伏，鼓手与贝斯形成密集对话，部分曲目通过留白让鼓与吉他独立构建律动。Pedro Lima的乐队展示了闷音吉他与套鼓的对抗，Africa Negra则展示了人声退场后纯粹器乐律动的延展能力。整体氛围充满热带岛国的湿润气息与非洲黄金年代的粗粝生命力。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 本文介绍长笛演奏家 Claire Chase 发起的 Density 2036 项目，这一历时二十四年的委约计划始于 2013 年，以瓦雷兹《密度 21.5》命名，意在为长笛这一乐器积累全新委约曲目，于 2036 年该项目百年纪念时收官。文章源自 I CARE IF YOU LISTEN 访谈，由 Julia Kuhlman 在项目中期进行对话，探讨 Chase 在委约机制、合作模式与艺术构想方面的实践思路。该项目属于当代古典音乐领域中的长篇委约实验，强调演奏家与作曲家之间的长期协作，为传统乐器注入新的创作语汇。然而，原文仅为简介式新闻摘录，缺乏对音乐本体、声音特征与作品细节的深入描述，信息量较为有限。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — A different step in direction for the band after a few line up changes and a period of inactivity, the band came back with a completely different vibe, but with familiar technical speeds and playing. The attempt at moving into a more progressive sound that they tried on Scruillous is more fully felt on this album, with vocalist Rody Walker almost sounding like a different singer, with a cleaner and less punky sound to his voice. At times his range does show some weakness, but the overall passion on this album from him and the rest of the band is very potent. Lyrically being a concept album based on American exceptionalism, it is very well crafted. The track I'd recommend is From The Sky.

items.body: Review by Prog Dog — This is a mellow, lush-sounding melodic rock instrumental album, with flashes of fusion and ambient textures around the edges. The band deliberately went for a distinctly "human" sound, avoiding excessive editing and resisting the urge to snap everything onto an electronic grid. In an age of compulsive digital perfection, there's something refreshing about leaving a little room for spontaneity?and even imperfection.Overall, this is a meditative album, ideally suited to enjoying while orbiting the Earth on a space station. There are a few moments with a jazz-fusion feel, including a track featuring electric violin, but for the most part the music inhabits its own spacious, melodic world. At times I was reminded of the solo work of Steve Howe and Steve Hackett, along with Robert Fripp, Pink Floyd, and even Pattern-Seeking Animals. But the further I got into Paradigms 2, the less useful those comparisons became. TAP seem to be defining a sound of their own.It's a little less edgy than their first album, Paradigms, but Paradigms 2 is more expansive and refined, with a broader and more varied sonic palette. It feels like a natural progression from TAP's debut, and a welcome addition to the growing body of work from this geographically separated partnership of musicians working across the USA, Canada, and England.The musicians (including several guests) are a treat throughout the album, bringing a diverse range of textures to the music. UK guitarist Suzi James (Fearful Symmetry) delivers flowing solos?sometimes with an Holdsworth-inspired flavour?along with some suitably proggy slide guitar. Texas-based Mark Cook adds the distinctive sound of the Warr guitar, mostly played fretless in the bass role. Together, they provide Paradigms 2 with plenty of instrumental colour without overwhelming its relaxed, atmospheric character.Key to the album's framework and beginnings, though, were the keyboard-based compositions Michael Jobborn sent out to the rest of the band. In a somewhat backwards fashion, the musicians took the pieces from there, massaging and developing them while gradually adding their own layers and contributions. This includes the competent and detailed drum work of Bill Bachman?whose grandfather, incidentally, was involved in the invention of the 33⅓ RPM LP.A couple of the tracks take a while to fully find themselves, including "A Hole in the Ground," although it has become one of my favourites on the album. It also features some surprisingly gentle vocals?a first for the band, although apparently not something they intend to make a regular feature.My one reservation is that Paradigms II could perhaps use a little more grit and sandpapery roughness to stretch its dynamics just a touch further. Whether that comes down to the compositions, recording, mixing, mastering, or some combination of all four, I'm not sure. I certainly can't fault the band for the achievement of putting this together largely as a home-studio project, if I have my facts straight. There's plenty here to admire. "4th Dimensional Wave" and the guitar solo work in "Wishful Solitude" provide a glimpse of what this kind of edge brings to the overall sound, adding even more texture and contrast to this spacious landscape.I can also attest that this album is a grower; the more I listened, the more it revealed itself.Overall: Paradigms II is a thoughtful, atmospheric progression from TAP's debut?an album that rewards relaxed listening and, preferably, a little distance out in Earth's orbit.4.25 out of 5 dog bones- or 4 out of 5 stars for the progarchives system.
items._genre: eclectic prog / instrumental rock / jazz-fusion / ambient
items._cn_summary: T.A.P第二张专辑《Paradigms II》由分散在美国、加拿大和英国的乐手远程协作完成，以键盘创作为框架，其余成员在此基础上叠加各自的器乐层次。Warr琴、电吉他、小提琴与鼓组之间的色彩搭配较为丰富，整体维持一种松弛、冥想式的氛围，试图在数字时代保留演奏中的即兴与不完美。评论者将其与Steve Howe、Steve Hackett、Robert Fripp及Pink Floyd的独奏作品相比较，但强调乐队逐渐走出参照、形成自身声音。部分曲目如《A Hole in the Ground》加入了轻柔人声，是乐队首次尝试。评论指出专辑动态张力略显温和，若能加入更多粗粝质感会更为完整。

items.body: Lords Of Acid release “Ich Will Nur Das” (I Just Want) on Metropolis Records on 11 September 2026, the group’s fourth single of the year. The frenetic dance track features a vocal by US electronic musician Mari Kattman, sung entirely in German. Ich Will Nur Das by Lords Of Acid Lords Of Acid founder Praga Khan describes the track as “basically a love song with a serious identity crisis. The verses are pure lust: hot, dirty, aggressive and completely unapologetic. Then the chorus suddenly turns into the romantic fantasy of a lovestruck teenager dreaming about eternal love.” Kattman is a Metropolis Records labelmate and a non-German speaker who has been touring on her own recent solo album, “Year Of The Katt.” “She was perfect for this song, as it is incredibly charming to hear her American voice attack these German lyrics,” Khan said. “We didn’t want her pronunciation to be too polished or perfect, as her accent gives the track extra personality. She also understood the contradiction at the heart of the song: one minute she sounds like she wants to devour you, the next she’s dreaming about everlasting love. It’s filthy and innocent at the same time, which is pretty much Lords Of Acid in a nutshell.” “Ich Will Nur Das” follows the previously released “Karaoke Superstar” featuring Princess Superstar, “Dream Boy” featuring Carla Harvey, and “El Mundo Esta Loco” featuring Tony & The Kiki. All four songs appear on “Mundo Bizarro,” the group’s new album, which streams digitally from 15 October to coincide with part two of the “Cheeky Freaky” US tour, with LP and CD editions following on 6 November. “Mundo Bizarro” tracklist: “Dream Boy,” “Dancing On The Flames,” “El Mundo Esta Loco,” “Dopamine War,” “Maximo Roboto,” “Ich Will Nur Das,” “City Of Angels,” “So Stoned Today,” “Karaoke Superstar,” “You’re Obscene” and “A Viking’s Heart.” About Lords Of Acid Lords Of Acid formed in Antwerp, Belgium in 1988 around Praga Khan and are recognised as one of the most influential acts to emerge from the hard-edged electronic dance music scene of that era, blending techno, acid house and industrial music with lyrics on sexuality, drug use and hedonism. The group debuted with the New Beat single “I Sit On Acid,” and its debut album “Lust” appeared in 1991, followed by further releases that saw the band become a staple of the Billboard dance and alternative charts. Carla Harvey, formerly of Butcher Babies, joined as singer in 2025. Having built a global following across a multi-decade touring career, Lords Of Acid remain one of the genre’s most recognisable names, with “Ich Will Nur Das” arriving ahead of the group’s next album, “Mundo Bizarro,” streaming digitally from 15 October 2026 ahead of LP and CD editions on 6 November.
items._cn_summary: 比利时老牌工业电子团体 Lords Of Acid 推出德语单曲，融合techno与acid house节奏，由美国电子音乐人 Mari Kattman 以非母语德语演绎。主创 Praga Khan 形容作品为带有身份危机的情歌——主歌部分充满欲望与攻击性，副歌则转向青少年式的浪漫幻想，形成肮脏与天真的并置。Kattman 美式口音未刻意打磨，保留了粗糙的个人特质。该单曲收入专辑《Mundo Bizarro》，此前已发行多首与不同客座歌手合作的曲目，整体延续团体一贯的性、药物与享乐主义主题。制作层面属工业舞曲常规路线，未见明显的声音设计突破或实验性结构，属于在既定框架内的稳定输出。

items.body: Breton producer Quinquis (Emilie Quinquis) has announced “scenes d’interieur”, her original soundtrack to Melanie Leray’s stage production of the same name. The five-track release comes out on 13 November 2026 via Mute. The multi-media production blends theatre and film as it follows Chloe, an actress preparing to perform the role of Nora in Henrik Ibsen’s “A Doll’s House.” The stage sections trace the breakdown of Chloe’s own relationship, while a parallel story shown on film covers her childhood, raised by a mother who survived domestic violence. Ibsen’s 1879 play, which caused a scandal on release for questioning the traditional roles of men and women in marriage, runs through both timelines, tying the production to themes of control and the search for emancipation. Quinquis’ score follows the two timelines, underscoring Chloe’s vulnerability, pain and strength as she navigates the violence of her stepfather as a teenager and of her husband as an adult in the present day. She uses modular electronics to score the live theatre performances and acoustic instrumentation for the film sections, extending the dialogue between past and present that runs through the production. The single “Lena” is an intimate piece where slow-moving synths give way to distant voices as the track builds through layers of emotion. The album was recorded on Ushant Island, off the coast of Brittany, where Quinquis lives, and features a track recorded with Amsterdam-based labelmate Desire Marea, “Inkanuko.” “scenes d’interieur” (catalogue number iMUTE703) carries five tracks: “Chloe,” “Nora,” “Puzuilhan,” “Inkanuko” and “Lena.” It follows Quinquis’ 2025 album “eor” and the 2024 single “Morwreg”, both also released via Mute. About Quinquis Quinquis is the project of Breton producer Emilie Quinquis, based on Ushant Island off the coast of Brittany. Her work moves between electronic and acoustic instrumentation, built around modular synthesis, field recording and a close relationship to the Breton coast where she lives. Quinquis released the “aer” EP and the album “SEIM” before “Morwreg” preceded her 2025 album “eor,” both issued via Mute. “scenes d’interieur,” her soundtrack to Melanie Leray’s stage production of the same name, follows in November 2026 and marks her first release built specifically for a theatre production, combining her modular electronic work for the live stage sections with acoustic instrumentation for the production’s film sequences.
items._genre: experimental electronic / ambient / field recording / modular synthesis

items.body: New Jersey industrial project Elektrikill, led by musician and producer Steve Vil, has released “Macabre Masquerade” through Evol Music Group. The 13-track album, Elektrikill’s second full-length of 2026, came out on September 1 and is built around a Halloween theme that runs through the whole tracklist. Macabre Masquerade by Elektrikill “Macabre Masquerade” combines new songs with reworked Elektrikill material, interludes and remixes credited to Kill Vector, Kontrol Phreak and an act billed as SPKTR. Kill Vector reworks “Ravenous” into “Ravenous (Rave Noose Mix),” Kontrol Phreak turns the “Monsters” track “(This Side Of) Parasite” into “Parasite (Darkest Fear Mix by Kontrol Phreak),” and SPKTR remixes “Drugs and Candy” as “Drugs and Candy (Trick Mixxx by SPKTR).” It has not been possible to confirm whether this SPKTR is the same act as The SPKtR, the project Graeme Revell of SPK leads with his son Robert J. Revell, or a separate, unrelated artist using a similar name. Across the album, Elektrikill moves between EBM, darkwave atmosphere, industrial-rock, electronic dance rhythms and cinematic horror, sequencing the tracks as one continuous set rather than a straight collection of horror-themed songs. “Macabre Masquerade” is out on CD and digital platforms, including Bandcamp and Spotify, with a vinyl LP edition available through elasticStage. About Elektrikill Elektrikill is the solo industrial project of Steve Vil, based in Alpha, New Jersey, and formed in 2021. Vil also works as a composer for film and television, with credits including “Grace and the Storm,” “Coma,” “The Pizza Man,” “No Clowning Around” and the theme music for the horror anthology series “Horror Shop Radio.” Elektrikill’s debut album, “Monsters”, arrived in 2023 and was named Industrial Album of the Year by NOTTHEAMP magazine. The project followed it with the EP “Propaganarchy!” (2024), the “Museum of Atrocity” EP (2026) and a contribution, “Titan of Will,” to the compilation “Electronic Saviors 7.” Elektrikill’s third album, “Küntzpiracy”, came out in May 2026 through Evol Music Group. With “Macabre Masquerade,” Elektrikill extends that catalog into a dedicated Halloween release built from new and reworked material.
items._cn_summary: 新泽西工业项目Elektrikill发布万圣节主题专辑《Macabre Masquerade》，收录13首曲目，融合EBM、暗潮氛围、工业摇滚、电子舞曲节奏与电影化恐怖元素。专辑将新歌与重新混音的作品编织成一个连续的整体概念，曲目之间穿插由Kill Vector、Kontrol Phreak和SPKTR等艺人制作的remix与interlude段落。项目主创Steve Vil同时从事影视配乐工作，将这种叙事感带入专辑结构中。整体策略偏向主题化、万圣节氛围的工业电子合辑，而非以单一原创概念驱动。在创新性与声音实验方面，乐评未提供足够的深度评论，难以判断其在工业子类型内部的突破程度。独立厂牌Evol Music Group发行，符合地下场景定位。
